question: Small-scale industries in India in 1950 were defined as all those industries in which the maximum investment amounted to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹5 lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1950, small-scale industries in India were defined based on the maximum investment limit.
 
• The maximum investment for small-scale industries was set at ₹5 lakh.
 
• This classification helped in identifying and promoting small-scale industries which were crucial for the economic development of India.
 
• Small-scale industries played a significant role in generating employment and reducing regional disparities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Small-Scale Industries:**

 
 
• Small-scale industries are those that are characterized by the small amount of investment in machinery and equipment.
 
• These industries are usually labor-intensive and require less capital investment.
 
 
 
• **Role in Economic Development:**
 
 
• They contribute significantly to the GDP of the country.
 
• They provide employment opportunities, especially in rural and semi-urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Government Support:**
 
 
• The government has provided various incentives, subsidies, and support schemes to promote small-scale industries.
 
• These measures include financial assistance, technical training, and marketing support.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Faced:**
 
 
• Lack of access to modern technology and skilled labor.
 
• Limited access to credit and financial resources.
 
• Competition from large-scale industries and imports.
